sections.theory:
Chapter Five: The present age and Islamic states

Teaching objectives

The purpose of this lesson is to enable the students that they:

1. becoming aware of the concepts of Islam, can solve those problems of the present age which the Muslim Ummah faces.

2. can know the limits and etiquette of residence and dwelling in Muslim countries and non-Muslim countries.

Religious, social and cultural difficulties of Muslims in non-Muslim states and their solution

At this time more or less 188 free and autonomous states exist on the globe. Of them 57 countries are Muslim. Most Muslim countries are found on the continent of Asia. Among them Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Kuwait, Pakistan, Turkey, Malaysia and Indonesia are more important. After this comes the number of the continent of Africa, where the number of Muslim countries is greater. Among them Sudan and Morocco are more important. There is no continent of the world where Muslims do not live. In some non-Muslim countries the number of Muslims is quite large, and in some Muslims are settled in comparatively small numbers. In the continent of Europe the only Islamic state is Bosnia.

In non-Muslim states Muslims face problems of various kinds, but among them religious, social and cultural difficulties are more important.

sections.title: باب 5 — متن (201)

paras.text: In the non-Muslim countries where Muslims are in a minority, they face difficulties of many kinds, but among them difficulties of a religious and religious-doctrinal nature are at the top of the list. In such countries Muslims cannot perform their religious acts of worship with much freedom. For example, where the population of Muslims is scattered, they cannot offer even the five daily prayers regularly in the mosques. Mosques either do not exist at all, or are so far from the house that going there five times is impossible. In the same way, on the occasion of Eid al-Adha animals for sacrifice are not easily available, and if Muslims arrange them from somewhere, difficulties come in slaughtering them. Moreover, in distributing the meat of the sacrifice too they have to face many difficulties. In the month of Ramadan al-Mubarak announcements of the times of sahri and iftar cannot be made. The prayers of the two Eids too have to be offered by going far, because the population of Muslims is small and also scattered. At the time of paying zakat too difficulty has to be faced. If deserving Muslims are not found among nearby neighbours, then the money of zakat has to be conveyed to far-off areas. For grappling with religious problems it is necessary that, as far as possible, Muslims live together, that is, in one area, so that in performing religious worship and rituals no difficulty of any kind is faced, and Muslims can perform their religious duties gracefully and with peace of heart.

sections.theory:
i. Religious difficulties

In the non-Muslim countries where Muslims are in a minority, they face difficulties of many kinds, but among them difficulties of a religious and religious-doctrinal nature are at the top of the list. In such countries Muslims cannot perform their religious acts of worship with much freedom. For example, where the population of Muslims is scattered, they cannot offer even the five daily prayers regularly in the mosques. Mosques either do not exist at all, or are so far from the house that going there five times is impossible. In the same way, on the occasion of Eid al-Adha animals for sacrifice are not easily available, and if Muslims arrange them from somewhere, difficulties come in slaughtering them. Moreover, in distributing the meat of the sacrifice too they have to face many difficulties. In the month of Ramadan al-Mubarak announcements of the times of sahri and iftar cannot be made. The prayers of the two Eids too have to be offered by going far, because the population of Muslims is small and also scattered. At the time of paying zakat too difficulty has to be faced. If deserving Muslims are not found among nearby neighbours, then the money of zakat has to be conveyed to far-off areas. For grappling with religious problems it is necessary that, as far as possible, Muslims live together, that is, in one area, so that in performing religious worship and rituals no difficulty of any kind is faced, and Muslims can perform their religious duties gracefully and with peace of heart.

ii. Social difficulties

In non-Muslim states Muslims have to face social difficulties of many kinds too, that is, societal difficulties. Since the society of Muslims is connected to a considerable extent with their religion, therefore in societal and social activities they have to face many difficulties, and Muslims, even if they want, cannot overlook them. So in social gatherings they have to face the time (of difficulty). In the same way in performing matters of marriage too many issues come up — for example the mixing of young men and women, the non-availability of suitable Muslim matches etc. Since the government is not of Muslims, therefore it too remains quite unsuccessful in solving these issues. جن غیر مسلم ممالک میں مسلمان اقلیت میں ہیں انہیں کئی قسم کی مشکلات درپیش ہیں لیکن ان میں دینی اور مذہبی نوعیت کی مشکلات سرِ فہرست ہیں۔ ایسے ممالک میں مسلمان اپنی مذہبی عبادات زیادہ آزادی سے ادا نہیں کر سکتے۔ مثلاً جہاں مسلمانوں کی آبادی بکھری ہوئی ہوتی ہے وہ پانچ وقت کی نماز بھی باقاعدگی سے مساجد میں ادا نہیں کر سکتے۔ مساجد یا تو سرے سے ہی نہیں یا پھر گھر سے اتنی دور ہیں کہ وہاں پانچ وقت جانا محال ہوتا ہے۔ اسی طرح عید الاضحیٰ کے موقع پر قربانی کے جانور آسانی سے دستیاب نہیں ہوتے اور اگر مسلمان کہیں سے بندوبست کر بھی لیں تو ان کو ذبح کرنے میں مشکلات آتی ہیں۔ علاوہ ازیں قربانی کا گوشت تقسیم کرنے میں بھی کئی مشکلات کا سامنا کرنا پڑتا ہے۔ رمضان المبارک کے مہینے میں سحر و افطار کے اوقات کے وقت افطاری و سحری کے اعلانات نہیں ہو سکتے۔ عیدین کی نمازیں بھی دور دراز جا کر ادا کرنی پڑتی ہیں کیونکہ مسلمانوں کی آبادی کم بھی ہوتی ہے اور بکھری ہوئی بھی ہوتی ہے۔ زکوٰۃ کی ادائیگی کے وقت بھی مشکل کا سامنا کرنا پڑتا ہے۔ اگر مستحق مسلمان قریبی ہمسائے میں نہ ملیں تو زکوٰۃ کے پیسے دور دراز علاقوں تک پہنچانا پڑتے ہیں۔ دینی مسائل سے نبرد آزما ہونے کے لیے ضروری ہے کہ جہاں تک ممکن ہو سکے مسلمانوں کو چاہیے کہ ایک ساتھ یعنی ایک ہی علاقے میں رہیں تاکہ مذہبی عبادات و رسومات کی ادائیگی میں کسی قسم کی دشواری کا سامنا نہ کرنا پڑے اور مسلمان اپنے مذہبی فرائض خوش اسلوبی اور اطمینانِ قلب سے ادا کر سکیں۔

ii۔ سماجی مشکلات

غیر مسلم ریاستوں میں مسلمانوں کو کئی قسم کی سماجی مشکلات یعنی معاشرتی مشکلات کا بھی سامنا کرنا پڑتا ہے۔ چونکہ مسلمانوں کا سماج کافی حد تک ان کے مذہب سے جڑا ہوا ہوتا ہے اس لیے معاشرتی و سماجی سرگرمیوں میں کئی مشکلات کا سامنا کرنا پڑتا ہے اور مسلمان چاہتے ہوئے بھی ان سے صرفِ نظر نہیں کر سکتے۔ مثلاً کھانے پینے کی اشیاء میں مسلمان حلال حرام کا بے حد خیال رکھتے ہیں جبکہ غیر مسلم جو چاہیں اور جیسے چاہیں کھا پی جاتے ہیں۔ چنانچہ معاشرتی اجتماعات میں انہیں وقت کا سامنا کرنا پڑتا ہے۔ اسی طرح شادی بیاہ کے امور کی ادائیگی میں بھی کئی مسائل آتے ہیں۔ مثلاً جوان لڑکے اور لڑکیوں کا اختلاط، مناسب مسلمان رشتوں کی عدم دستیابی وغیرہ چونکہ حکومتِ وقت مسلمانوں کی نہیں ہوتی اس لیے وہ بھی ان مسائل کے حل میں خاصی ناکام رہتی ہے۔ مسلمانوں کو چاہیے کہ وہ امدادِ باہمی کے اصولوں کو مدِنظر رکھتے ہوئے

sections.content:
i. Religious difficulties

In the non-Muslim countries where Muslims are in a minority, they face difficulties of many kinds, but among them difficulties of a religious and religious-doctrinal nature are at the top of the list. In such countries Muslims cannot perform their religious acts of worship with much freedom. For example, where the population of Muslims is scattered, they cannot offer even the five daily prayers regularly in the mosques. Mosques either do not exist at all, or are so far from the house that going there five times is impossible. In the same way, on the occasion of Eid al-Adha animals for sacrifice are not easily available, and if Muslims arrange them from somewhere, difficulties come in slaughtering them. Moreover, in distributing the meat of the sacrifice too they have to face many difficulties. In the month of Ramadan al-Mubarak announcements of the times of sahri and iftar cannot be made. The prayers of the two Eids too have to be offered by going far, because the population of Muslims is small and also scattered. At the time of paying zakat too difficulty has to be faced. If deserving Muslims are not found among nearby neighbours, then the money of zakat has to be conveyed to far-off areas. For grappling with religious problems it is necessary that, as far as possible, Muslims live together, that is, in one area, so that in performing religious worship and rituals no difficulty of any kind is faced, and Muslims can perform their religious duties gracefully and with peace of heart.

ii. Social difficulties

In non-Muslim states Muslims have to face social difficulties of many kinds too, that is, societal difficulties. Since the society of Muslims is connected to a considerable extent with their religion, therefore in societal and social activities they have to face many difficulties, and Muslims, even if they want, cannot overlook them. For example, in things to eat and drink, Muslims keep extreme care of halal and haram, whereas non-Muslims eat whatever they want and however they want. So in social gatherings they have to face the time (of difficulty). In the same way in performing matters of marriage too many issues come up — for example the mixing of young men and women, the non-availability of suitable Muslim matches etc. Since the government is not of Muslims, therefore it too remains quite unsuccessful in solving these issues. Muslims should, keeping in view the principles of mutual help …
